statement: Let n = len(transactions). For 0 <= i < n, let name_i, time_i, amount_i, city_i be the components of transactions[i] as described in the preconditions. Define invalid(i) as: amount_i > 1000, or there exists j with 0 <= j < n, j != i, such that name_j = name_i, city_j != city_i, and |time_i - time_j| <= 60. Whenever the function returns a result r, r is a permutation of the list [transactions[i] | 0 <= i < n and invalid(i)]. Equivalently, for every byte vector v, the number of occurrences of v in r equals the number of indices i with invalid(i) and transactions[i] = v.
preconditions: transactions is a slice of byte vectors with len(transactions) <= 1000. For every i with 0 <= i < len(transactions), transactions[i] is an ASCII string of the form name_i + ',' + time_i + ',' + amount_i + ',' + city_i, where name_i and city_i are strings of lowercase English letters of length 1 to 10, time_i is a decimal integer with 0 <= time_i <= 1000, and amount_i is a decimal integer with 0 <= amount_i <= 2000.
